name: Kin Landholding
description: Defines the balance between household cultivation communal obligation and chiefly claims.
option_description: Household plots remain embedded in reciprocal obligations to kin and local assemblies.
note: This is a gameplay abstraction from settlement and enclosure evidence and does not reconstruct a common British land code.

name: Przeworsk Household Production
description: Defines obligations connecting metalworking households exchange and the local muster.
option_description: Specialist production remains dispersed among settlements and household networks.
note: Archaeological production evidence is translated into a dispersed-workshop option without inventing guild law or a unified Przeworsk constitution.

name: Dyakovo Settlement Obligations
description: Defines household labor owed to defended promontory settlements and river approaches.
option_description: Households maintain earth timber and access works through negotiated local obligations.
note: This is a settlement-defense adapter and does not reconstruct a common law across the late-Dyakovo distribution.

name: Gorodets Fortification Duties
description: Defines the seasonal labor and muster used at defended forest-steppe settlements.
option_description: Local households rotate watch and repair duties rather than sustain a permanent garrison.
note: Fortification evidence supports the mechanic while the exact composition chronology and use of individual sites remain variable.

name: Northern Seasonal Round
description: Defines reciprocal access to fishing hunting and gathering places across a mobile annual cycle.
option_description: Households negotiate access and obligations across river lake forest and coastal resource zones.
note: This ecological adapter deliberately avoids imposing later ethnic territories property law or one subsistence pattern.

name: Forest-River Exchange
description: Defines obligations and safe conduct among households using linked river corridors.
option_description: Local exchange specialists coordinate movement without a centralized customs apparatus.
note: The option is a regional exchange adapter and does not claim a common law among materially distinct horizons.

name: Kama Offering Custody
description: Defines responsibility for local offering places and communal ritual deposits.
option_description: Ritual specialists and household leaders maintain offering places through local obligations.
note: Glyadenovo evidence anchors the option while its extension remains conservative and does not posit a regional priestly hierarchy.

name: Pyanobor Mortuary Custody
description: Defines kin obligations surrounding cemeteries commemoration and deposited metalwork.
option_description: Households maintain burial places and reciprocal commemorative duties.
note: The law is a mortuary gameplay adapter rather than a reconstruction of doctrine inheritance or a single Pyanobor identity.

name: Sargat Retinue Obligations
description: Defines how leading households assemble mounted and foot followers for bounded campaigns.
option_description: Prestige exchange and household ties sustain temporary forest-steppe followings.
note: Status differentiation in cemeteries supports a retinue adapter but not a permanent army hereditary caste or unified Sargat command.

name: Altai Contact Exchange
description: Defines obligations among valley communities and brokers moving goods through Inner Asian contact routes.
option_description: Local leaders protect exchange through reciprocal gifts and negotiated access.
note: The option models contact without turning material similarities into evidence of conquest occupation or one caravan state.

name: Kulay Specialist Casting
description: Defines access to metal skill molds and exchange among dispersed casting households.
option_description: Specialists retain household control of casting knowledge while exchanging finished objects along river routes.
note: The option is grounded in the material horizon but does not invent guild regulation or a unitary Kulay political economy.

name: Hillfort Muster
description: Defines the temporary concentration of fighting households around defended gathering places.
option_description: Local retinues and household levies assemble for bounded campaigns rather than serving as a permanent army.
note: Hillforts had highly variable uses; this option is a regional military adapter and not proof of universal garrisons or one levy constitution.

name: Sanctuary Obligations
description: Defines the ritual obligations mediated by local sacred specialists and gathering places.
option_description: Communities sustain local vows feasts and sacred deposits without a centralized priestly state.
note: The option permits bounded religious differentiation while explicitly avoiding a uniform druidic constitution.

name: Pastoral Obligations
description: Defines reciprocal household duties around herding food storage and livestock wealth.
option_description: Kin groups coordinate herding and redistribution without a centralized fiscal code.
note: This is an AD 1 pastoral gameplay adapter and deliberately does not backdate medieval Irish legal tracts.

name: Seaway Muster
description: Defines the obligation of coastal households to provide crews and fighting followings.
option_description: Fishing and exchange crews can be gathered for short maritime campaigns while remaining locally based.
note: Ptolemy's coastal ordering supports maritime orientation but not a uniform island-wide naval law or quantified fleet.

name: Votive Obligations
description: Defines communal support for local ritual specialists and sacred deposition.
option_description: Communities sustain local vows feasts and deposits through reciprocal household contributions.
note: Archaeological ritual evidence is converted into a bounded gameplay option without claiming a centralized priesthood or uniform doctrine.

name: Assembly Deliberation
description: Defines how leading lineages and armed households negotiate public decisions.
option_description: Proposals are debated by leading speakers and accepted or rejected through the gathered households.
note: Tacitus offers a Roman outsider's compressed account; this option represents negotiated assent without asserting identical assemblies everywhere.

name: Retinue Obligations
description: Defines the gifts hospitality and service binding martial companions to leading households.
option_description: Leaders sustain fighting companions through reciprocal prestige gifts and shared campaigning.
note: The option is a bounded military adapter and does not project medieval vassalage or a universal permanent warband into AD 1.

name: Grove Obligations
description: Defines communal support for groves vows divination and local ritual mediation.
option_description: Households sustain sacred places and ritual specialists through reciprocal local obligations.
note: Tacitus supports a broad ritual pattern but not one pantheon priestly corporation or uniform sacred law.

name: Amber Custody
description: Defines communal claims over the collection exchange and movement of coastal amber.
option_description: Coastal and riverine households broker amber through reciprocal exchange networks.
note: This option models archaeological exchange and Tacitus's later amber notice without inventing prices roads monopolies or a merchant corporation.

name: Hillfort Obligations
description: Defines household duties for defended gathering places stores and seasonal musters.
option_description: Local households provision defended centres and gather fighting bands for bounded emergencies.
note: Hillfort form and use varied across the Brushed Pottery zone; this does not imply permanent garrisons or one centralized command.

name: Ancestral Burial Obligations
description: Defines household support for locally distinctive barrow stone-circle and tarand cemeteries.
option_description: Kin groups maintain burial places offerings and commemorative obligations through local custom.
note: The option deliberately preserves regional mortuary difference and treats archaeological cultures as uncertain gameplay frames rather than named states.

name: Regional Satrapy Governance
description: Defines the court's reliance on regional military and administrative intermediaries.
option_description: The king governs through regional elites whose authority remains politically important.
note: This is a gameplay adapter for a politically composite Indo-Scythian realm and does not reconstruct a uniform satrapal constitution.

name: Late Hellenic Court Governance
description: Defines the court and city-elite balance of the remaining Indo-Greek kingdom.
option_description: The last Indo-Greek court relies on the cooperation of its urban elites.
note: This is a gameplay adapter for a late Hellenistic court and urban setting, not a reconstructed constitutional text.

name: Council Governance
description: Defines the authority of the leading clans within a ganasangha.
option_description: Leading clans govern through a republican council rather than a hereditary royal court.
note: This is a gameplay adapter for attested ganasangha republican forms and does not reconstruct a specific constitution or membership roll.

name: Civic Cult Practice
description: Defines the relationship between Rome's public cult and locally observed religious practices.
option_description: Roman public rites coexist with many locally observed cults under imperial order.
note: This is a technical tolerance adapter for plural cult practice; it is not a claim of modern religious freedom or a denial of particular coercions and exclusions.

name: Unfree Status
description: Defines the legal permission for enslavement and manumission within the Roman legal order.
option_description: The Roman legal order permits enslavement while retaining multiple pathways to manumission.
note: This records a legal-status baseline only; it does not quantify enslavement or manumission or reduce diverse provincial practices to one uniform experience.

name: Royal Canal Endowments
description: Defines the court's support for irrigation works and monastic grants.
option_description: Royal patronage supports canals and the communities connected to them.
note: This is a gameplay adapter for attested royal canal endowments and does not reconstruct a general Anuradhapura water-law code.

name: Civic Status
description: Defines the relationship between imperial citizenship and subject communities.
option_description: Provincial communities retain differentiated civic status before the universal grant of 212.
note: The later Constitutio Antoniniana is reserved for its AD 212 history path.

name: Military Recruitment
description: Defines the balance between regular troops and broader levies.
option_description: The Roman field force is centred on long-service regular formations.
note: This is a pre-M7 administrative adapter; exact unit rosters and levy composition remain M7 work.

name: Commandery Administration
description: Commanderies and centrally appointed officials structure the Han state.
option_description: The court governs through commandery and county administration.
note: The estate preferences are technical UI adapters rather than a social classification of Han officeholders.

name: Noble Autonomy
description: Defines the contractual balance between the Arsacid king and powerful noble houses.
option_description: The Arsacid court governs through an accommodation with its great houses.
note: This legal adapter represents the political relationship rather than a reconstructed written statute.

name: Client Governance
description: Defines the balance between a local royal court and its imperial patron.
option_description: The client king preserves local authority while relying on Roman recognition and support.
note: This is a political adapter for Roman client relationships and not a claim that Mauretania and Nabataea used one written constitution.

name: Kushite Royal Authority
description: Defines the court-centred authority of the Kushite rulers.
option_description: Royal authority is maintained through the Kushite court and its religious legitimacy.
note: This is a gameplay adapter for royal authority and does not reconstruct a Kushite legal code.

name: Confederation Governance
description: Defines the balance between the chanyu and the constituent Xiongnu clans.
option_description: The chanyu rules through a confederation whose clans retain substantial leverage.
note: This legal adapter represents confederation politics rather than a written Xiongnu statute.

name: Early Korean Kingship
description: Defines the royal and leading-house balance in Goguryeo.
option_description: The king governs through a developing royal court and leading houses.
note: This is a conservative adapter pending a dedicated early Korean institutional pass.

name: Tribal Governance
description: Defines the relationship between a king and the leading kin groups.
option_description: The ruler governs with the consent and influence of leading kin groups.
note: This is a shared technical adapter and not a claim that Marcomannic and Catuvellaunian institutions were identical.

name: Sub-King Governance
description: Defines the balance between a regional Iranian court and the Arsacid political order.
option_description: A regional king governs through local elites while retaining an Arsacid-facing political relationship.
note: This is a gameplay adapter for a regional court and not a reconstructed Parthian legal text.

name: Buffer-Kingdom Governance
description: Defines the courtly balance needed by a frontier kingdom between larger powers.
option_description: The frontier court preserves internal authority while navigating competing imperial interests.
note: This technical law represents borderland politics without claiming a common written constitution for Armenia and Osroene.

name: Temple Administration
description: Defines the relationship between the Herodian court and the Jerusalem priesthood.
option_description: The Temple's priesthood remains a major civic and religious institution under the Herodian ethnarch.
note: The administrative-law surface is a gameplay adapter and does not reconstruct the exact legal authority of the high-priesthood.

name: Augustan Coinage
description: Defines the imperial monetary standard of gold and silver coinage.
option_description: Gold aurei and silver denarii provide the imperial monetary standard.
note: Engine coinage terms approximate a mixed Roman circulation; denomination ratios and mint jurisdictions are not reconstructed.

name: Wuzhu Coinage
description: Defines the standard copper cash used by the Western Han state.
option_description: Cast Wuzhu cash remains the Han monetary standard at the AD 1 start.
note: The coinage modifiers reuse the installed copper-coin contract and do not claim an exact Han fiscal model.

name: Regional Court Governance
description: Defines a bounded relationship between a regional monarch and leading court figures.
option_description: The monarch governs through a court whose exact offices are not reconstructed.
note: This is a generic gameplay adapter for documented monarchies and not a claim of a shared constitutional tradition.

name: Advanced Chiefdom Governance
description: Defines the balance between a chief and the authorities that sustain a developing polity.
option_description: A chief governs through leading kin and local authorities without a reconstructed state bureaucracy.
note: This is a technical adapter for Aksum's emerging polity rather than a claim about an exact chiefly constitution.

name: Settled Town-Cluster Governance
description: Defines the civic coordination of a settled urban community.
option_description: Leading urban households coordinate a settled community without an invented monarch or formal city constitution.
note: This is a technical adapter for Djenné-Djenno's settled town cluster and not a documented constitutional reconstruction.
